reason: E1 and E2 directly support the formation of a metastable W(Cu) solid solution via CPF-induced melting and rapid quenching, and E2 shows increased radiation resistance in CPF-treated W-Cu. However, the cited evidence does not compare CPF-treated samples against a conventional molten Cu infiltration baseline, nor does it quantify void reduction or thermal transport improvements, leaving the comparative performance premise unsupported.
premises: CPF treatment with ~100 μs pulse and ~35 J/cm² energy density can melt and mix W and Cu at the near-surface
Ultra-fast quenching (10^6–10^7 K/s) after CPF produces a metastable W(Cu) solid solution with a distorted lattice
The W(Cu) solid solution traps excess vacancies, suppressing void formation and phase separation
CPF-treated W-Cu structures exhibit increased radiation resistance compared to untreated W
The proposed CPF treatment will yield reduced voids and phase-separated regions relative to conventional molten Cu infiltration
